analogy: Rentvesting is the Australian strategy of renting where you want to LIVE while owning investment property where it makes financial sense — essentially separating the location decision from the investment decision. It's grown popular among young professionals in Sydney and Melbourne priced out of their preferred suburbs. The math can work compellingly: someone paying $1,800/week rent in Sydney's eastern suburbs (where buying equivalent would be $2.5M) can instead rent there AND own a $800k Brisbane investment property yielding 4.5% gross, with the investment property's interest tax-deductible. If mortgage on the Sydney buy would have been $14,000/month, renting Sydney at $7,800/month plus owning Brisbane at $1,780/month net = $9,580 total, freeing up $4,420/month for additional investing. Over 10 years that's $530,000+ at 7% returns. But the key complexity is the PPOR (Principal Place of Residence) CGT exemption — owner-occupied homes are CGT-free when sold, while investment properties face CGT (with 50% discount after 12 months). If Sydney grew 4%/year over 10 years, that $2.5M home becomes $3.7M = $1.2M capital gain, all CGT-free. The Brisbane investment property at 5%/year = $1.3M, $500k gain, $250k taxable after 50% discount, $92k tax at 37% MTR — net $408k. So on headline capital gains, buying PPOR often wins by $500k-$1M+ over a decade. But — and this matters — rentvesting frees up substantial monthly cash that, disciplined-ly invested in share markets (8-10% returns), can offset the CGT disadvantage. Whether it actually does depends entirely on whether the rentvester invests the difference vs spending it on lifestyle. The strategy works well for: high earners in expensive cities, DINK couples or singles with career mobility, early-career professionals who'll move for jobs, those who genuinely prefer flexibility. It works less well for: families with kids (school zones, stability matter more), those who emotionally need homeowner status, risk-averse personalities uncomfortable with rental uncertainty, those in tight rental markets with rising rents. The practical execution: buy cash-flow-positive investment property in a different market (regional growth corridors common — Brisbane, Adelaide, Perth growth corridors yield 4-6% vs Sydney/Melbourne 2-3%), use professional property management (~7-10% of rent for interstate), invest surplus cash in diversified share portfolio, review annually. The exit strategy matters — plan 2-3 years ahead for CGT timing, consider converting investment to PPOR if eventually moving there, use low-income years to crystallize gains. For any Denaro client considering rentvesting, $500-1,500 of accountant + financial adviser consultation is worth it — the tax structure, CGT planning, and long-term strategy choices have $50k+ swings. The strategy is neither magic wealth-building nor financial self-harm — it's a legitimate alternative path that fits some situations and not others.

snippet: Rentvesting = renting where you live (often lifestyle location) while owning investment property elsewhere. Pros: more affordable lifestyle in expensive cities, tax-deductible investment property interest, flexibility, potentially wealth-build faster. Cons: PPOR exemption lost (CGT on investment gains), no stable housing, emotional challenges. Works well for: high earners in Sydney/Melbourne priced out of preferred suburbs, DINK professionals, career mobility.
